messages:
mira: Heads up — SCIM deprovisioning is failing for multiple Okta tenants after yesterday's RBAC role rename. A bunch of users are stuck in `pending_deprov` and the provisioning worker shows KMS decrypt failures. :warning:

devon: Ugh. Any logs or sample user IDs? Is this only Okta or also Azure?

mira: Only seeing this on Okta so far (two orgs). Example user: alice+corp@example.com. Worker log attached below.

samir: pasted log snippet:
```
2026-03-23T10:12:07Z provisioning-worker ERROR user=alice+corp@example.com request_id=01F8ZKZ0KXK3Z0Y0 kms:Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException
caused_by: kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345 alias/ri-provisioning-key
stack: /srv/provisioner/deprov.go:124 handleDeprov -> requeue after backoff
```

jen: Did the KMS key policy change during the RBAC work? I remember infra rotated a few aliases yesterday.

mira: We rotated the alias as part of the org key hygiene job around 01:00 UTC. Rotation pipeline reported success, but there was a short window where the alias pointed to the new key before IAM bindings finished. Not sure if that lines up.

kms-bot: kms-rotation: alias `alias/ri-provisioning-key` re-pointed at key `arn:aws:kms:...:key/ef01-789a` by infra-svc at 2026-03-22T01:03:12Z (event id evt-9f2b).

oncall-lambda: @oncall-lambda I see audit logs missing deprovision entries for the affected users — looks like the worker error occurs before the service emits the final audit row. That would explain customer audit gaps. :eyes:

devon: Ok. Two parallel things: 1) we need a short-term customer workaround (manual deprovision) 2) we need a plan to reprocess the backlog safely and ensure audit trails. For workaround, run this (ops-only):
```
rictl provisioning deprovision --user alice+corp@example.com --force --dry-run=false --log-level debug
```
I'll run it once we confirm the KMS permissions are back.

jen: We cannot use a "master" key fallback for compliance. Suggest re-encrypting backlog items with the new key after we confirm decrypt rights, then requeue. But we must avoid double-auditing.

samir: I can write a small migration that attempts KMS decrypt with the old key, then rewrap to the current key and mark the record with the original_request_id. Steps:
- run a read-only pass to enumerate `pending_deprov` keys and record request_ids
- attempt decrypt with key versions in rotation history
- for items that decrypt, re-encrypt against current key and push to normal queue
- emit a single audit event with field `migration_origin: "kms-rewrap-2026-03-23"` to allow dedupe downstream

mira: That plan sounds good. Estimated run time for org with ~3k pending entries?

samir: ~20-30 min for one org (single worker), we'll throttle to avoid DB load.

devon: Also add a safety: if audit row for request_id already exists, skip to avoid duplicates. We need to ensure audit is idempotent by request_id.

jen: Make sure legal/infosec sign off on the migration annotation before running. I'll loop them in.

mira: I'll notify affected customers with a brief "we detected stuck deprovisions due to key rotation; we're running a migration and will re-run deprovision; no user access lingering beyond expected window."

devon: I'll own the one-off migration script and the run. Samir can peer-review and handle the KMS rewrap bits.

samir: Will draft the script now. Posting repo PR in 15m.

mira: Thanks. Please ping #cust-status when you start. :thumbsup:

jen: Adding a postmortem checklist: update rotation runbooks to include a small delay after alias re-point before RBAC or provisioning-sensitive jobs run; add an automated smoke test that runs a dummy deprovision through the pipeline after alias change.

devon: Agreed. Also add an observability alert: spikes in `provisioner.kms.decrypt.errors > 5m` to page SRE.

mira: Cool. I'll follow up with infra to capture the exact rotation timeline.
